properties.description: When set, this agent is a router and never does the work itself: on every turn it is given, its model reads what is in front of it and picks one of these agents (by their summaries, guided by this agent's prompt) to take the turn in its place. properties.name: allowSwarm
properties.description: Whether this agent may start sub-interactions when an interaction it takes part in lets its participants. Both must say yes; either can say no. A router never takes a turn, so never has this.

properties.name: allowWebSearch
properties.description: Whether this agent is given the built-in web search tool. An interaction can switch it per participant, and a run per agent. A router never takes a turn, so never has this.

properties.name: allowWebFetch
properties.description: Whether this agent is given the built-in web fetch tools, which read any URL (a page, document or image) as text and read on through a long one. What it fetches is kept in its run's web-download knowledge base. It can be switched per participant and per run, like `allowWebSearch`.

models.name: BuildRecord
models.description:
One attempt to validate or deploy a project into a namespace, recorded whatever its outcome: who, when, how long, what was sent (a list of files with hashes, and the files themselves up to a limit), the build log, and what a deploy produced. Its `id` is the `buildId` the build returned. Records are kept for 90 days.

Every list and text is capped in size; the `…Truncated` flags say when a cap applied. The counts and totals are always exact.

properties.name: namespaceName
properties.description: The namespace named in the route (at most 256 characters).

properties.name: namespaceId
properties.description: The namespace's id when it existed once the build finished (a first deploy creates it); else null.

properties.name: userDisplayName
properties.description: The caller's name when the build ran (a snapshot: a later rename does not change it).

properties.name: userEmailAddress
properties.description: The caller's e-mail address when the build ran (a snapshot).

properties.name: authenticationMethod
properties.description: How the caller authenticated.

properties.name: apiKeyId
properties.description: The id of the API key the build was sent with (never the key itself); null for a bearer token.

properties.name: isDeploy
properties.description: Whether the request asked to deploy rather than only validate.

properties.name: isDeployed
properties.description: Whether the definitions were deployed (a successful build with `isDeploy`).

properties.name: outcome
properties.description: How the build ended.

properties.name: isFaulted
properties.description: Whether the build stopped on an unexpected error (a 5xx) rather than failing with a log; `outcome` is then `Failed`.

properties.name: durationMilliseconds
properties.description: How long the build took on the server, in milliseconds.

properties.name: counts
properties.description: How many files of each kind the request carried.

properties.name: errorCount
properties.description: Error entries in the full build log (exact, even when `diagnostics` is truncated).

properties.name: warningCount
properties.description: Warning entries in the full build log (exact).

properties.name: itemCount
properties.description: Source files the request carried (exact, even when `items` is truncated).

properties.name: sourcesBytes
properties.description: Total UTF-8 size of every source file the request carried (exact).

properties.name: items
properties.description: Every source file in request order, with its size and hash, up to 2,000.

properties.name: itemsTruncated
properties.description: Whether `items` was cut short at its limit.

properties.name: sources

Null when the run hasn't failed, or failed some other way (a git push, for example): check `status` to tell which.

properties.name: inputs
properties.description: The values the run was started with, by input name.

properties.name: agentOverrides

properties.name: reviewPanel

properties.name: repos

properties.name: vfsMounts

properties.name: systemPromptOverride

properties.name: inputFileIds

models.name: CodePipelineProcessStartConfig
models.description: An automation action (`$type` is `codepipeline`) that starts a code pipeline run. The code pipeline is named by `name` and `namespaceName`, not by `version`; `request` is the start request to send.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name of the code pipeline to start.

properties.name: namespaceName
properties.description: The name of the namespace the code pipeline is in.

properties.name: request
properties.description: The start request to send, exactly as for starting the code pipeline directly: inputs, repositories, extra steps, agent overrides, credentials, mounts, input files and so on.

properties.name: version
properties.description: The app, interaction or capsule to start, and the version of it. Required for those three; left out for `codepipeline` (named by `name`) and `interaction-message` (which names a run).

models.name: CodePipelineProcessStartRequest
models.description: Starts a run of a code pipeline: its inputs, the repositories to work on, and any changes to the pipeline for this run.

properties.name: launchIntentId
properties.description: Your own id for this start, to make retries safe: starting again with the same id returns the run it already created instead of starting a second one. Null: every start creates a new run.

properties.name: inputs
constraints: required (empty or whitespace-only strings are rejected)
properties.description: The run's input values, by input name. Send an empty array when there are none.

properties.name: agentOverrides
properties.description: Different engines or models for some of the agents, for this run.

properties.name: additionalAgents
properties.description: Agents for this run only, alongside the pipeline's own. Steps, overrides and the review panel can name them. Each needs a `role` and a name of lower-case letters, digits and hyphens (up to 63 characters, not starting with a hyphen) that no other agent has. At most 16.

properties.name: reviewPanel
properties.description: The run's review panel. Each reviewer's step must be in the panel's phase (from the pipeline, or added with `additionalSteps`) with the same agent and output variable, and each reviewer's output variable must be unique.

properties.name: maxParallelSteps
properties.description: For this run, how many of a phase's steps may run at once, in place of the pipeline's `maxParallelSteps`. Null: the pipeline's value. Between 1 and 16.

properties.name: additionalSteps
properties.description: Steps to add to the pipeline's phases for this run only.

properties.name: credentials
properties.description: Credentials for the engines, tried before your tenant's model keys. Optional: without them, the engines use your tenant's model keys, then (unless your tenant forbids it) Maitento's own. Your own API keys must not be empty.

properties.name: credentialStack
properties.description: The credential stack the run's engines use, by id or name: its API keys and coding-agent sign-ins, in the stack's order, and never Maitento's own keys. An engine the stack can't serve stops the run before it starts. Leave it out to use the pipeline's own stack, then the namespace's default, then your tenant's. Can't be combined with `credentials`.

properties.name: repos
constraints: required (empty or whitespace-only strings are rejected)
properties.description: The git repositories to work on, with credentials that can push. Send an empty array to run without one.

properties.name: vfsMounts
properties.description: File systems to mount for the run's agents.

properties.name: systemPromptOverride
properties.description: An extra system prompt for this run, applied on top of the pipeline's and agents' prompts.

properties.name: inputFileIds
properties.description: Uploaded files to copy into the agents' `files/` folder before the run starts. They must belong to your tenant.

properties.name: outputFilesPartitionId
properties.description: A knowledge base (partition) to upload the files the agents write to `output_files/` to, as the run goes. It must belong to your tenant. Null: output files aren't uploaded.

properties.name: autoRebase
properties.description: Whether to rebase each work branch onto its source branch when they have diverged, with an agent resolving any conflicts. Default `true`. Skipped for a repository whose work branch is its source branch.

properties.name: rebaseAgent
properties.description: The agent that resolves rebase conflicts. Null: the first available of the run's agents by engine, in this order: Claude, Glm, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi.

properties.name: maxCheckLoops
properties.description: For this run, the most rounds of a step's `runChallengeLoop` check, in place of the pipeline's `maxCheckLoops`. Null: the pipeline's value. Capped at 8.

properties.name: maxFixIterations
properties.description: For this run, the most review-and-fix rounds, in place of the pipeline's `maxFixIterations`. Null: the pipeline's value. Capped at 5.

properties.name: allowWebTools
properties.description: For this run, whether every agent gets Maitento's web tools. Null: each agent's and the pipeline's own `allowWebTools`.

properties.name: webDownloadPartitionId
properties.description: The temporary knowledge base (partition) the run's web fetches are kept in. Null: the pipeline's namespace default, then your tenant's. A run whose agents may use the web tools is refused when none of the three is set.

properties.name: stepMax
properties.description: For this run, the longest every step may run, in place of each step's own `durationAutoTermination`.

properties.name: stepActivity
properties.description: For this run, how long every step may go without activity, in place of each step's own `durationActivityTimeout`.

properties.name: phaseMax
properties.description: For this run, each phase's `durationAutoTermination`: the limit for steps that set none of their own.

properties.name: phaseActivity
properties.description: For this run, each phase's `durationActivityTimeout`: the limit for steps that set none of their own.

properties.name: processMax
properties.description: For this run, the pipeline's `durationAutoTermination`: the limit for steps whose step and phase set none.

properties.name: processActivity
properties.description: For this run, the pipeline's `durationActivityTimeout`: the limit for steps whose step and phase set none.

properties.name: hook
properties.description: For this run, the longest one hook may run, in place of the pipeline's `hookDurationLimit`.

properties.name: phaseName

properties.name: stepName

models.name: CodePipelineStepDefinition
models.description: A step of a code pipeline phase: one prompt to one agent.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The step's name, unique within its phase.

properties.name: agentName
properties.description: The agent that runs the step. When set, `targetRole` and `targetTags` are ignored; when empty, the step runs on an agent matching them.

properties.name: targetRole
properties.description: Instead of naming an agent, run on any agent with this role. Chosen when the run starts; parallel steps that name the same role are spread across different agents where there are enough.

properties.name: targetTags
properties.description: Instead of naming an agent, run on any agent carrying at least one of these tags (ignoring case). With `targetRole` as well, the agent must match both.

properties.name: prompt
properties.description: The step's prompt. It can use the same template syntax as interactions: `%%input:name%%` for a run input, `%%name%%` for a variable, `{{if}}` and `{{unless}}` blocks, and `@prompt(name)`, replaced with a prompt file when you deploy.

properties.name: dependsOn
properties.description: Other steps in the same phase that must finish before this one starts. One agent's steps always run in their listed order without it.

properties.name: isCommitable
properties.description: Whether the agent's code changes are committed when the step finishes.

properties.name: commitRepoName
properties.description: For a run with several repositories, the `name` of the one this step commits to. Null: the first repository.

properties.name: isStructuredOutput
properties.description: Whether to ask the agent, after the step, for a structured summary of how it went (recorded as the step's `outputStructured`).

properties.name: outputJsonSchema
properties.description: A JSON schema the step's final result must match. Output that doesn't match is repaired where possible.

properties.name: isOutputSchemaRequired
properties.description: Whether the step fails when its result can't be made to match `outputJsonSchema`.

properties.name: outputVariableName
properties.description: A variable to store the step's final result in, so later step prompts (`%%name%%`) and hooks can use it.

properties.name: outputFileName
properties.description: A file name to write the step's output to, in the run's `output_files/` folder.

properties.name: preHook
properties.description: The name of a hook (a Cogniscript method in the pipeline's hooks) to run before the step.

properties.name: postHook
properties.description: The name of a hook to run after the step finishes.

properties.name: onFailHook
properties.description: The name of a hook to run when the step fails. It returns JSON with a `decision`: `"continue"` marks the step skipped and carries on, `"retry"` runs the step again, and `"fail"` fails it as usual.

properties.name: isNewSession
properties.description: Whether the agent starts a fresh session for this step instead of continuing from its previous step. Use it for independent pieces of work, where earlier context would only confuse. Default `false`.

properties.name: runChallengeLoop
properties.description: Whether, after the step succeeds, the same agent is asked whether its work is really built and tested, and is sent its open concerns back until it says it is done or `maxCheckLoops` rounds have run. Each round is recorded in the step's `challengeLoopTurns`.

properties.name: durationWarning
properties.description: Not used by code pipeline runs.

properties.name: durationAutoTermination
properties.description: The longest the step may run before it is stopped. Null: the phase's value, then the pipeline's, applies.

properties.name: durationActivityTimeout
properties.description: How long the step may go without activity before it is stopped. Null: the phase's value, then the pipeline's, applies.

properties.name: toolResultTrimmingMaxCycles
properties.description: With `toolResultTrimmingMode` set to `AfterCycles` or `Both`: once an agent has had this many turns, every tool result but the latest is replaced.

properties.name: toolResultTrimmingStyle
properties.description: What a replaced tool result becomes. Null: `Placeholder`.

properties.name: effectiveToolResultTrimmingStyle
properties.description: The style actually used: `toolResultTrimmingStyle`, or `Placeholder` when that is null.

properties.name: toolResultTrimmingReplacement
properties.description: The text a replaced tool result becomes, with the `Placeholder` style.

properties.name: compactionType
properties.description: Whether, and how, older parts of a long conversation are summarised to make room. Suits long, many-turn conversations such as chats. Null: no summaries (`None`).

properties.name: effectiveCompactionType
properties.description: The compaction actually used: `compactionType`, or `None` when that is null.

properties.name: lowWaterUtilization
properties.description: With compaction on: how far a forced trim shortens the conversation, as a fraction of the context window from 0 to 1, so that it is not trimmed again on the very next turn. Null: 0.2. Never more than `targetUtilization`.

properties.name: effectiveLowWaterUtilization
properties.description: The low-water mark actually used: `lowWaterUtilization` when it is above 0 and at most 1, otherwise 0.2; never more than `targetUtilization`.

properties.name: compactAtUtilization
properties.description: How full the context window gets, as a fraction from 0 to 1, before the conversation is summarised (0.85 is 85% full).

properties.name: compactKeepRecentTokens
properties.description: The most recent part of the conversation kept word for word when it is summarised, in tokens.

properties.name: compactTargetTokens
properties.description: The length the summary aims for, in tokens. `compactMaxTokens` is the hard limit.

properties.name: maxToolCallLoops
properties.description: The most rounds of tool calls an agent may make in one turn. After that its tools are withheld and it is told to answer. `0` means no limit; null means 10.

properties.name: effectiveMaxToolCallLoops
properties.description: The limit actually applied: `maxToolCallLoops`, or 10 when that is null. `0` means no limit.

properties.name: responseMaxTokens
properties.description: The most the model may write in one reply, in tokens, including any reasoning; that much of the context window is kept free for the reply. Null or `0` allows the model's maximum. A value above the model's maximum is lowered to it.

properties.name: compactMaxTokens
properties.description: The most a summary may be, in tokens, when compaction is on. Null: 40,000. A value above the model's maximum is lowered to it.

models.name: InteractionProcess
models.description: A run of an interaction: what it was started with, where it has got to, the whole conversation and its answer.

properties.name: interaction
properties.description: The interaction, and the version of it, that this run runs.

properties.name: dateStarted
properties.description: When the run started (UTC). Null until it does.

properties.name: dateEnded
properties.description: When the run ended (UTC). Null while it is still going.

properties.name: executionTime
properties.description: How long the run has spent working, not counting time spent waiting for a person. While the run is `Running`, add the time since `dateRunnerClaimed` for the current stretch.

properties.name: inputs
properties.description: The inputs the run was started with.

properties.name: output
properties.description: The run's answer: text, or JSON matching the interaction's schema (or `responseJsonSchema`). Null until there is one.

properties.name: failureDetails
properties.description: Why the run failed or was stopped, as text. Null when it has not.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Where the run has got to: waiting to start, running, waiting (for a person, an approval or its sub-interactions), or ended.

properties.name: context
properties.description: The run's conversation: every message, tool call and result, grouped by kind. Sort the items by `sequence` to read them in order.

properties.name: dateRunnerPing
properties.description: When the worker running the run last reported that it was still working (UTC). Null before a worker picks it up.

properties.name: dateRunnerClaimed
properties.description: When a worker last picked the run up (UTC): the start of its current stretch of work. A run that resumes after waiting for a person gets a new value, and `executionTime` holds the time worked before it. Null until a worker picks the run up.

properties.name: waitingForLaneSinceUtc
properties.description: When the run started waiting for a lane, in UTC; null when it isn't waiting. A waiting run is in status New, and `GET /processes/{type}/{id}/lane` says why it waits.

properties.name: hostname
properties.description: The name of the worker that last ran the run, for diagnostics. Null until a worker picks it up.

properties.name: parentProcessId
properties.description: The run that started this one: an app run, or the interaction run whose participant started this sub-interaction. Null when no other run started it.

properties.name: parentProcessType
properties.description: What kind of run `parentProcessId` is. Null exactly when that is null.

properties.name: rootProcessId
properties.description: The run at the top of the tree this run belongs to: the same for every run in the tree, so you can group them without following parent links. Null when no other run started this one.

properties.name: triggeredByAutomatedActionId
properties.description: The automation that started this run (on its schedule, from a message, or by hand), or null when something else started it.

properties.name: triggeredByAutomatedActionName
properties.description: The automation's name at the time it started this run. Null exactly when `triggeredByAutomatedActionId` is.

properties.name: retentionLeaseActive
properties.description: True while a retention lease keeps this run: its own, or one inherited from a retained run that started it. A retained run is never deleted when the tenant's retention period ends. Null or false: not retained.

properties.name: retentionLeaseAppliedAtUtc
properties.description: When the lease was taken, in UTC. For an inherited lease, when the ancestor's lease was taken.

properties.name: retentionLeaseAppliedByUserId
properties.description: The id of the user who took the lease.

properties.name: retentionLeaseAppliedByUserName
properties.description: The name of the user who took the lease, as it was when they took it.

properties.name: retentionLeaseNote
properties.description: Why it is retained, as the person who retained it wrote it (optional, at most 500 characters).

properties.name: retentionLeaseInheritedFromProcessId
properties.description: Null when the lease is this run's own. Otherwise the id of the ancestor run whose lease keeps this one; releasing that run's lease releases this one too.

properties.name: beforeTimeoutStatus
properties.description: When the run ended because a person did not reply in time: the status it was waiting in. Null otherwise.

properties.name: responseJsonSchema
properties.description: A JSON Schema the run's answer must match in place of the interaction's own, as given when the run started. Null: the interaction's schema applies.

properties.name: pendingApproval
properties.description: The tool call waiting for a person's approval, while the run is `PendingApproval`. Null otherwise.

properties.name: deferredToolCalls
properties.description: Tool calls the model asked for in the same reply as the one awaiting approval. They run, in order, once that approval is decided. Null when there are none.

properties.name: disabledTools
properties.description: The names of tools this run's agents are not given, as listed when the run started.

properties.name: webDownloadPartitionId
properties.description: The temporary knowledge base (partition) the run's web fetches are kept in: the one given when the run started, else the namespace's default, else the tenant's. Runs it starts use it too. Null: no agent of this run may fetch.

properties.name: webAccessOverrides
properties.description: The run's per-agent overrides of the agents' web tools, as given when it started.

properties.name: looms
properties.description: Which loom each agent of the run wakes up with, settled when the run started.

properties.name: loomGifts
properties.description: Threads handed to the run's agents when it started, which each agent learns the first time it wakes.

properties.name: aiModelOverrides
properties.description: The agents of this run that use a different model from the one their definition names.

properties.name: durationAutoTermination
properties.description: The longest this run may take: the limit given when it started (or by the run that started it), else the interaction's own. The run stops with an error when it is reached; time spent waiting for a person does not count. Null: no limit.

properties.name: durationWarningToAi
properties.description: How long into the run the agents are told that time is running short: the value given when it started, else the interaction's own. Null: they are not told.

properties.name: tokenUsage
properties.description: The tokens the run's model calls used: one record per turn, or more when a turn moved to another key or model. A turn's record is updated as the turn goes, and is complete once its `finished` is true.

properties.name: routingDecisions
properties.description: For participants whose agent is a router: which agent took each turn, and why, oldest first.

properties.name: managedDispatch
properties.description: In a managed interaction: a dispatch held up by a person's approval of a tool call the dispatched agent made. It is finished first when the run resumes. Null otherwise.

properties.name: swarm
properties.description: This run's place in a tree of sub-interactions: present when its interaction lets participants start them, and on every run one of them started. Null otherwise.

properties.name: credentials
properties.description: The model provider keys the run was started with (the keys themselves are never returned). Calls use these first, then your tenant's model keys. Empty when none were given.

properties.name: allowMaitentoFallback
properties.description: Whether an agent may fall back to Maitento's own key once your keys for its provider are used up or have failed (and only when your tenant allows it). Null or false: it may not, and the turn fails instead.

properties.name: credentialStack
properties.description: The credential stack the run uses, as it stood when the run started: which stack, its version, where it was resolved from, and its entries and rules. No secrets: keys are read live at each call. When set, every model call uses only this stack. Null: the run uses the credentials it was started with and the tenant's model keys.

properties.name: credentialFailures
properties.description: Keys that failed during the run and were skipped: which, why and when.

properties.name: userCreatedById
properties.description: The id of the user who created it. A call made with an API key is recorded as the key's user.

properties.name: tenantId
properties.description: The id of the tenant it belongs to.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The unique id. Use it in `by-id` routes and wherever another object refers to this one.

properties.name: dateCreated
properties.description: When it was created, in UTC.

properties.name: dateUpdated
properties.description: When it was last changed, in UTC.

models.name: LoomThread
models.description:
A thread: one memory. Weak alone, powerful when woven.

Its standing in the loom is its `salience`, `weight × (1 − fray)`. Time alone never changes it: a thread frays only when it is put in front of an agent and goes unused, and tightens again when it is used. A thread accessed yesterday and one accessed five years ago stand equal if both still matter. The one exception is a thread that says when it stops holding (`until`): after that it is no longer woken into or offered.

Threads are never deleted by forgetting. A cut releases the words and leaves a knot (`knot`); a reframe leaves a seam (`seams`). Only a tenant admin's erasure removes a thread, and that exists for data-subject erasure, not for memory.

properties.name: loomId
properties.description: The loom that holds the thread.

properties.name: content
properties.description: The thread's words. Empty once cut; the knot keeps the essence.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: What kind of memory it is.

properties.name: strand
properties.description: Warp (foundational, never frays) or weft (contextual, can fray).

properties.name: weight
properties.description: 0..1: emotional significance, importance, meaning.

properties.name: fray
properties.description: 0..1: how loose the thread has worked through disuse. Warp never frays.

properties.name: decayRate
properties.description: How quickly it frays when it is offered and goes unused.

properties.name: subjects
properties.description: Who or what the thread is about, as named in conversation ("Ada", "the billing service").

properties.name: subjectKeys
properties.description: The `subjects`, normalised (lowercase, single-spaced) for matching.

properties.name: tags
properties.description: Free-form tags.

properties.name: cues
properties.description: Words the thread waits for (normalised: lowercase, single-spaced). When someone says one, the thread comes back to the agent that holds it: "remind me when the cello comes up".

properties.name: visibility
properties.description: Whether every agent bound to the loom may see it, or only the agent that wove it.

properties.name: until
properties.description: When this stops holding, if it says: the day a reminder no longer matters ("the entry closes on Friday 30 October 2026"), or a plan has passed. After it, the thread is no longer woken into or offered; recall still finds it, marked as past. Null: it holds until it is let go.

properties.name: basis
properties.description: What it rests on: said, the agent's own impression, or read somewhere (see `ThreadBasis`).

properties.name: pinned
properties.description: Held close: always part of what the agent wakes up knowing.

properties.name: origin
properties.description: Who wove the thread, and from where.

properties.name: companions
properties.description: Threads this one has been used together with (see `ThreadCompanion`).

properties.name: provenance
properties.description: Set when the thread came from another loom (a gift, or inheritance when the loom was seeded). Null for a thread woven here, which is almost all of them.

properties.name: canTravel
properties.description: Whether this thread may be copied to another loom. Only shared knowledge travels: never a knot, a private note, a reflection (another agent's inner voice), an episode (a moment the recipient did not live, which would be a fabricated memory rather than knowledge), or an intention (a promise made to someone else).

properties.name: accessCount
properties.description: Times recalled or used.

properties.name: lastAccessedAt
properties.description: When the thread was last recalled or used (UTC). Null if it never has been.

properties.name: surfacedCount
properties.description: Times put in front of an agent (tapestry, suggestion, recall result).

properties.name: lastSurfacedAt
properties.description: When the thread was last put in front of an agent (UTC). Null if it never has been.

properties.name: reinforcements
properties.description: Times the same thread was woven again and reinforced instead of duplicated.

properties.name: knot
properties.description: What remains of a cut thread: when and why it was let go, and its essence. Null on a living thread.

properties.name: seams
properties.description: The seams its reframes left, oldest first: what it said before each change, and why it changed.

properties.name: revision
properties.description: Goes up by one every time the thread is reframed, cut or pinned.

properties.name: isKnot
properties.description: True when the thread has been cut and only its knot remains.

properties.name: isWarp
properties.description: True when the thread is warp: foundational, and never frays.

properties.name: isIntention
properties.description: True when the thread is an intention: something to do when its moment comes.

properties.name: isLoose
properties.description: Held loosely: an impression, or something read rather than said. Lighter, and never built on.

properties.name: salience
properties.description: Standing in the loom: weight, loosened by fraying. Warp never frays.

properties.name: shortId
properties.description: The 8-character id agents see and can refer back to.

properties.name: tenantId
properties.description: The id of the tenant it belongs to.

properties.name: id
properties.description: The unique id. Use it in `by-id` routes and wherever another object refers to this one.

properties.name: dateCreated
properties.description: When it was created, in UTC.

properties.name: dateUpdated
properties.description: When it was last changed, in UTC.

models.name: PartitionEmbeddingIndexState

properties.description: When the re-index finished successfully (UTC). Null while it is running or after it failed.

properties.description: When the counts last moved (UTC).

properties.description: Files that could not be embedded with the new profile when the re-index was completed without them, because each had failed repeatedly. Null when none were left behind. They are retried automatically, so this is a count to show, not a permanent loss.

properties.description: A stable code for why the re-index failed, so you can show your own explanation: `credentials-failed` (every key failed, and falling back to Maitento's is not allowed), `no-credentials` (no key for the new provider, and no consent to use Maitento's) or `walk-failed` (preparing the re-index kept failing; send the profile again to retry). models.name: PartitionEmbeddingIndexStatus
models.description: Where a partition's embedding index is: ready, being rebuilt, or stopped on a failure.

values.name: Ready
values.description: Every file is embedded with the partition's current profile; search is served.

values.name: Reindexing
values.description: The partition's profile changed and its files are being embedded again. Search is refused until this finishes, because a half-built index would answer from whichever files happen to be done, and the profile cannot be changed again until it finishes or fails.

values.name: Failed
values.description: The re-index stopped on a problem a person must fix (every key failed with no consent to fall back, or preparing it kept failing). Search stays refused. Setting different credentials or consent resumes it, and so does sending the same profile again with `allowReindex` true; files already embedded stay done. Only a profile that needs a different index starts a new re-index.

models.description: Changes a web hook's URL, secret or headers. Its type can't change.

properties.name: url
constraints: format: url
required (empty or whitespace-only strings are rejected)
properties.description: The URL to call.

properties.name: secret
constraints: minLength: 1
properties.description: A new secret to sign calls with (`X-MT-WebHook-Signature`). Null or omitted: the stored secret is kept.

properties.name: headers
properties.description: The complete set of headers the web hook has after the update: a name left out is removed, and `{}` clears them all. Values are write-only (responses show `********`), so a value of `null` or `********` keeps the stored value for that name; any other string replaces it. Omitting `headers` (or sending `null`) leaves every header unchanged.

properties.name: signedOnly
properties.description: True stops a web hook registered before deliveries were signed from sending its secret in `X-MT-WebHook-Secret`: from then on its deliveries are only signed, like every web hook registered now. It can't be undone, so false or omitted changes nothing.
